results.title: PIMoE: Towards Efficient MoE Transformer Deployment on NPU-PIM System through Throttle-Aware Task Offloading
results.abstract: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) technique holds significant promise for scaling up Transformer models. However, the data transfer overhead and imbalanced workload hinder efficient deployment. This work presents PIMoE, a heterogeneous system combining processing-in-memory (PIM) and neural-processing-unit (NPU) to facilitate efficient MoE Transformer inference. We propose a throttle-aware task offloading method that addresses workload imbalance between NPU and PIM, achieving optimal task distribution. Furthermore, we design a near-memory-controller data condenser to address the mismatch of sparse data layout between NPU and PIM, enhancing data transfer efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that PIMoE achieves $4.5 \times$ speedup and $13.7 \times$ greater energy efficiency compared to the A 100, and $1.4 \times$ speedup over a state-of-the-art MoE platform.

results.title: Optimizing Distributed LLM Serving through Request Scheduling and Key-Value Cache Sharing
results.venue: International Conference on Parallel and Distributed Systems
results.abstract: The widespread deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) is often constrained by the significant computational and memory demands of the inference process. A critical bottleneck in distributed serving systems arises from the redundant processing of requests that share common prefixes, such as system prompts or few-shot examples. Traditional contentagnostic load balancers fail to exploit these redundancies, leading to inefficient resource utilization and increased latency. This paper introduces a dynamic, prefix-aware request scheduling system designed to optimize distributed LLM serving. Our approach intelligently routes incoming requests to specific GPU workers by analyzing prompt content and matching it with the resident Key-Value (KV) caches across the cluster. By colocating requests with shared prefixes, our system maximizes KV cache reuse, minimizes expensive prefill computations, and enables more efficient batched attention operations at the worker level. We implemented and evaluated this scheduler on a 12 -node GPU cluster using a real-world chatbot workload. The results demonstrate the profound impact of content-aware scheduling: our system increased the aggregate prefill throughput by over 144 % and reduced the median Time-to-First-Token by over 40 % compared to a conventional Round-Robin policy. These performance gains are a direct result of an 82 % relative increase in the prefix cache hit rate, validating our approach as a highly effective and cost-efficient strategy for enhancing the throughput and responsiveness of large-scale LLM services.

results.title: MultiPrune: Extreme Compression of Visual Tokens for Large Multimodal Models via Training-Free Multi-Cue Pruning
results.venue: International Conference on Virtual Reality and Visualization
results.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have demonstrated remarkable potential in various multimodal tasks, such as image captioning and visual question answering. However, their computational cost is prohibitively high due to the extensive visual data involved. Recent studies reveal significant redundancy in visual tokens, making token pruning an emerging research focus. Most of previous works either need intense retraining of the models, or with reduced performance for the extreme compression. In this paper, we propose an efficient training-free visual token pruning approach for MLLMs. It utilizes three cues as follows: attention scores, token similarity and information entropy. Our method MultiPrune adopts multistage pruning from the early stages of layers to choose the most informative tokens and can even produce a high acceleration with no need for any extra training or architecture modification. In extensive experiments on 11 popular datasets and a variety of tasks (ranging from visual recognition to reasoning, OCR and multimodal scientific question answering), MultiPrune can still retain as few as 12.5 % of the original visual tokens with only a small accuracy drops by 1.38 %. MultiPrune consistently outperforms existing compression methods while its trainingfree, plug-and-play capability ensures strong generalizability and practicality for vision-language tasks in realistic scenarios.

results.title: HarMoEny: Efficient Inference of MoE Models
results.venue: IEEE International Parallel and Distributed Processing Symposium
results.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models offer computational efficiency during inference by activating only a subset of specialized experts for a given input. This enables efficient model scaling on multi-GPU systems that use expert parallelism without compromising performance. However, load imbalance among experts and GPUs introduces waiting times, which can significantly increase inference latency. To address this challenge, we propose HarMoEny, a novel solution to address MoE load imbalance through two simple techniques: (i) dynamic token redistribution to underutilized GPUs and (ii) asynchronous prefetching of experts from the system to GPU memory. These techniques achieve a near-perfect load balance among experts and GPUs and mitigate delays caused by overloaded GPUs. We implement HarMoEny and compare its latency and throughput with four MoE baselines using real-world and synthetic datasets. Under heavy load imbalance, HarMoEny increases throughput by 37%–70% and reduces time-to-first-token by 34%–41%, compared to the next-best baseline. Moreover, our ablation study demonstrates that HarMoEny’s scheduling policy reduces the GPU idling time by up to 84% compared to the baseline policies.

results.title: Tensor Parallelism for State-Space Models
results.venue: IEEE International Conference on Distributed Computing Systems
results.abstract: State space models (SSMs) have recently emerged as an effective backbone for sequence modeling and are increasingly used in large language models (LLMs), particularly in long-context regimes. However, serving performance for SSMbased LLMs is constrained by the capabilities of a single GPU, motivating GPU-parallel implementations to scale capacity and improve performance. While tensor parallelism (TP) is a wellestablished mechanism for scaling LLM inference, it is difficult to employ TP for SSMs due to their distinct structure: they include a sequence-wise recurrent state update and local mixing whose efficiency depends on keeping state and key intermediates local. In this paper, we present a communication-efficient tensor-parallel design and implementation for SSM inference that overcomes the systems challenges of parallelizing SSMs by introducing an SSM cache to reuse per-layer recurrent state and by designing an SSM-aware partitioning to preserve local state updates while avoiding unnecessary synchronization. Our experimental evaluation of four representative SSM-based LLMs (Mamba, Mamba-2, Falcon-Mamba, and Zamba) on two GPU platforms (NVIDIA A6000 and A100) shows that our tensor-parallel SSM inference on 2 and 4 GPU setups improves throughput by $\sim 1.4-3.9 \times$ compared to single-GPU inference. Our design also allows us to handle $\sim {2}-{4} \times$ larger batch sizes and output sequence lengths due to efficient memory usage compared to Data Parallelism and single-GPU inference.

results.title: Adapting FlexLLMGen to Qwen3 Dense and Mixture-of-Experts Models
results.venue: 2026 10th International Conference on Electronic Information Technology and Computer Engineering (EITCE)
results.abstract: FlexLLMGen is a representative heterogeneous-memory inference framework, but its original implementation is centered on OPT-style dense decoders and cannot directly run recent Qwen3 dense and mixture-of-experts (MoE) checkpoints. This paper presents a two-stage adaptation of FlexLLMGen to Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-30B-A3B. Beyond compatibility itself, the main technical contribution is a scheduler-preserving migration abstraction that separates model-family adaptation into three reusable adapters: configuration translation, checkpoint normalization, and operator replacement, with differential verification as a built-in validation layer. Starting from the original OPT-oriented assumptions in FlexLLMGen, we introduce a Qwen3-specific configuration path, a unified checkpoint-normalization pipeline from Hugging Face safetensors to runtime-consumable numpy weights, and runtime support for RoPE, grouped-query attention, SwiGLU, Q/K normalization, router execution, and shared experts. Experiments cover memory, latency, throughput, sequence-length sensitivity, and a dense output-fidelity proxy under single-GPU heterogeneous offloading. For Qwen3-0.6B, changing from no offloading to CPU/disk-heavy offloading reduces peak GPU memory from 2.039 GB to 1.206 GB, a 40.9% reduction, while end-to-end throughput drops from 9.50 to 5.85 tokens/s at the 64/64 setting. For Qwen3-30B-A3B, the analytical direct-loading baseline is about 60 GB in bf16/fp16 parameter storage, whereas the adapted Flex offloading path completes execution with only 1.716–2.334 GB peak GPU memory, corresponding to about 96.1%–97.1% memory reduction across tested prompt/generation lengths. These results show that the proposed approach makes FlexLLMGen compatible with both Qwen3 dense and Qwen3 MoE models, preserves its offloading-based memory advantage, and offers a reusable migration recipe for other modern dense and sparse decoder families.

results.title: Enhancing Large Language Model Inference Efficiency via Lookahead Cache Filtering
results.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
results.abstract: The large Key-Value (KV) cache is a significant challenge in deploying Large Language Models (LLMs). Current research addressing these issues employs cache compression techniques, which we find suffer from information loss and the "lost-in-the-middle" problem. We propose the Lookahead Cache Filtering (LCF), which retains the full cache in host memory to keep complete details, using the Important Key-Value Lookahead Prediction by Approximate Sorting and the Gather-based Matrix Multiplication on CPU, to filter important KV cache to reduce the overhead of loading cache to GPU and improve the throughput of inference. Finally, we use the Multi-Scale Pyramid Information Fusion mechanism to enhance information fusion to further improve the effectiveness of inference results. Experiments demonstrate that LCF effectively maintains accuracy without introducing additional latency while reducing memory requirements. Our code will be available on GitHub1.

results.title: WAN Cache: Wide-Area Multi-Tier KV Cache Based Inference Acceleration Networks
results.abstract: The widespread deployment of Large Language Model (LLM) applications has triggered a massive increase in concurrent inference requests, which poses significant challenges to inference network architectures and systems. As LLM inference expands from single data center to wide-area distributed infrastructure, three key challenges need to be addressed: insufficient KV Cache storage capacity, lack of effective cross-regional cache reuse, and inefficient wide-area transmission. This paper proposes WAN Cache, wide-area multi-tier KV Cache based inference acceleration networks built on a local-edge-cloud hierarchical architecture. Within this framework, this paper presents three core mechanisms: cache-affinity inference request distribution, wide-area multi-tier cache scheduling, and wide-area high-throughput transmission. Through the coordination of these mechanisms, WAN Cache establishes a KV Cache-centric network that optimizes request latency and cache hit rates to scale inference networks across geographically distributed environments. Transmission experiments show that WAN Cache maintains over 75 Gbps throughput under 160 ms Round-Trip Time and 0.1% packet loss in laboratory tests, and achieves approximately 90% bandwidth utilization on a 1,000 km production link in field tests. Caching simulations on real-world LLM workloads show that three-tier cache reduces Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) by up to 48.8% and improves hit rate by up to 42.9 percentage points (pp) over single-tier cache, while cross-cluster sharing reduces TTFT by up to 47.6% and improves hit rate by 32.0 pp over private cache. These results demonstrate that WAN Cache achieves near-local inference performance across wide-area deployments.

results.title: Crowd: An KV Cache Eviction Policy Which Uses Crowd Information to Select Evicted Key-Value Pairs
results.venue: 2024 4th International Conference on Computer Science and Blockchain (CCSB)
results.abstract: Although large language models have been widely applied in various aspects of daily life, it is worth noting that, in addition to their substantial demand for computational resources, they also require an exceptionally large amount of GPU memory. This is because, aside from the model weights, the key-value cache must also be stored in GPU memory, and the size of this cache increases with the batch size and sequence length, becoming a significant bottleneck in inference. In this paper, we introduce an innovative method for optimizing key-value (KV) cache, significantly reducing its memory usage. Through experimental validation, we observed that the higher the similarity between query vectors, the higher the similarity between the key vectors they attend to. Additionally, experiments showed that the vectors most similar to the current query vector are concentrated within its local window size. Based on these findings, we propose a new KV cache eviction policy called Crowd, which can dynamically select the necessary key-value pairs for inference without requiring model retraining or fine-tuning. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superiority of Crowd during both the pre-filling and autoregressive decoding stages.

results.title: Accelerated Dynamic Quantization and Semantic Pruning for Large Language Models on Edge Communication Devices
results.venue: 2025 4th International Joint Conference on Information and Communication Engineering (JCICE)
results.abstract: Large language models have demonstrated strong performance in natural language processing tasks, but their high computational and memory demands hinder deployment on edge devices. To address this, we propose a lightweight inference acceleration method combining three techniques: dynamic activation quantization, semantic-aware pruning, and input-adaptive pruning scheduling. The method dynamically adjusts quantization parameters based on per-layer activation distributions to mitigate accuracy loss from outliers. It further incorporates word embeddings and syntactic features to assess token importance, enabling fine-grained, semantics-driven token pruning. Pruning strength is adaptively adjusted based on input length, improving adaptability across scenarios. Experiments show that our method achieves up to $2.8 \times$ inference speedup without compromising model performance, outperforming standalone weight quantization or attention pruning.

results.title: Language Modeling With Factorization Memory
results.abstract: We propose Factorization Memory, an efficient recurrent neural network (RNN) architecture that achieves performance comparable to Transformer models on short-context language modeling tasks while also demonstrating superior generalization in long-context scenarios. Our model builds upon Mamba-2, enabling Factorization Memory to exploit parallel computations during training while preserving constant computational and memory complexity during inference. To further optimize model efficiency and representational capacity, we develop a sparse formulation of Factorization Memory that updates only a subset of recurrent states at each step while preserving the strong performance of its dense counterpart. To our knowledge, this represents the first RNN architecture that successfully combines sparse memory activation with competitive performance across both short and long-context settings. This work provides a systematic empirical analysis of Factorization Memory in comparison to Transformer and Mamba-2 architectures.
